root_cause.text: The team driver’s NETDEV_UNREGISTER cleanup path called `dev_set_mtu()` on a slave device in `team_port_del()`, which incorrectly emitted a `NETDEV_CHANGEMTU` notifier during unregister and caused re-entrant refcounting/use-after-unregister behavior.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `team_port_del()` to take a `unregister` flag and, for unregistering slaves, replaces `dev_set_mtu(port_dev, port->orig.mtu);` with `netdev_lock_ops(port_dev); __netif_set_mtu(port_dev, port->orig.mtu); netdev_unlock_ops(port_dev);`, while `team_device_event()` now calls `team_del_slave_on_unregister()` for `NETDEV_UNREGISTER` instead of the normal deletion path; the CVE description explicitly says to “avoid NETDEV_CHANGEMTU event when unregistering slave” and shows the problematic call chain through `dev_set_mtu()` into `call_netdevice_notifiers_mtu`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an unregister flag to port deletion so the removal path can distinguish device unregistration from ordinary port removal.
intent_record.what: The function prototype for `team_port_del` was changed from `static int team_port_del(struct team *team, struct net_device *port_dev)` to `static int team_port_del(struct team *team, struct net_device *port_dev, bool unregister)`, adding a new boolean parameter named `unregister`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, callers can now indicate whether removing a port should also be treated as part of device unregistration versus a normal port deletion path. This enables the function to distinguish between different removal contexts and adjust its behavior accordingly in later code.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix port removal to restore MTU safely during unregister by using the locked internal MTU setter instead of dev_set_mtu().
intent_record.what: In team_port_del(), the unconditional call to dev_set_mtu(port_dev, port->orig.mtu) was replaced with a conditional: when unregister is true, the code now acquires the netdev ops lock, calls __netif_set_mtu(port_dev, port->orig.mtu), and releases the lock; otherwise it keeps using dev_set_mtu(port_dev, port->orig.mtu).
intent_record.how: This changes MTU restoration during port removal so that the unregister path updates the device MTU through the lower-level internal helper while holding the appropriate lock, avoiding an unsafe or invalid MTU change during teardown, while preserving the previous behavior for non-unregister removal.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update team teardown to call team_port_del() with an explicit false flag so port removal during uninitialization uses the correct cleanup behavior.
intent_record.what: In team_uninit(), the call to team_port_del() inside the port_list iteration was changed from team_port_del(team, port->dev) to team_port_del(team, port->dev, false).
intent_record.how: At runtime, the uninitialization path now passes an explicit false flag to team_port_del(), altering the deletion behavior for each port during cleanup. This changes how port removal is performed during team teardown, likely disabling an additional side effect or special handling that the previous two-argument call implied through a default path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Split slave removal into normal and unregister-time paths so port deletion can handle device teardown correctly.
intent_record.what: The call site in team_del_slave() was changed from team_port_del(team, port_dev) to team_port_del(team, port_dev, false). A new function, team_del_slave_on_unregister(), was added; it retrieves the team private data, asserts RTNL, and calls team_port_del(team, port_dev, true).
intent_record.how: The port removal path now distinguishes between a normal slave deletion and a removal that happens during device unregister. The added boolean argument lets team_port_del() adjust its behavior based on whether the port is being explicitly removed or is disappearing because the underlying net_device is going away.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use a dedicated unregister-time slave removal helper to handle device teardown correctly.
intent_record.what: In the NETDEV_UNREGISTER case of team_device_event(), the call to team_del_slave(port->team->dev, dev) was replaced with team_del_slave_on_unregister(port->team->dev, dev).
intent_record.how: At runtime, device unregistration now uses a dedicated slave-removal path instead of the सामान्य slave deletion function, likely ensuring unregister-specific cleanup or ordering is handled correctly when a device is removed.
